label: copy-phase input token d
explanation: Fires when the input token is d during the copy phase (when the model reads back its own echoed d). It never fires on d in the original phase or at the delimiter, and it essentially never fires on any other token (only a few weak activations on u or 0 at the last step). Activation is usually weaker when d is echoed at the first copy step (recall_idx 1, i.e. first_tok d), and about 12% of copy-phase d inputs are inactive, mostly early in the copy phase. The strongest activations come late in the copy phase, often when d is the next-to-last original token or the d is repeated (dd); for a repeated dd the first echoed d is stronger than the second. Dev: P 0.88, R 1.00, F1 0.94.

issues: The core predicate holds up. Test: P 0.879, R 1.000, F1 0.936, mass recall 1.000. Only 6 test activations fall outside it (weak u/0, about 0% of mass). The inactive copy-phase d steps are spread out with no clear pattern. The inactive rate is about 9-12% in every slice tried: in_count==1 P 0.90, in_count>=2 P 0.79, prev_tok digit P 0.92, next_out digit P 0.87, n_digits 0 vs >=2 P 0.88 vs 0.87, L>=7 P 0.89. Misses on dev and test show no token or history pattern.

The explanation's magnitude claim is wrong. 'The strongest activations come late in the copy phase, often when d is the next-to-last original token' is contradicted by quartile coverage. d at to_go==0, which is exactly the next-to-last original token being read back, covers 0.236/0.241/0.176/0.092 of quartiles 1-4, so it is strongly depleted in the top quartile. t>=14 is also depleted (0.217 -> 0.140). The top quartile is instead enriched for to_go>=3, mid copy phase with outputs still to come (0.403 -> 0.574). The claim was generalised from the max-activating examples, which happen to be L=9 at to_go 0 (that subset is only 3% of activations).

'About 12% of copy-phase d inputs are inactive, mostly early in the copy phase' is overstated. recall_idx==1 has 27% inactive, about 4.5k of about 10.9k dev false positives (around 42%). The remaining ~58% sit at recall_idx>=2, where about 8.6% are inactive. L==3 is also weak (P 0.31), but it is tiny (870 steps).

Claims that check out: zero activation in the original and delimiter phases. Weaker activation at recall_idx 1: share of mass 0.121 vs share of activations 0.151, top-quartile coverage 0.08 vs 0.23 in the bottom quartile. In repeated dd the first echoed d is stronger, as the top examples show. The reported refinement F1s match (recall_idx>=2 gives 0.88).
The non-d exceptions are not only 'at the last step'. Test misses include u at steps 9, 11 and 16, right before an echoed d. They are negligible in mass.

Not upheld because one factual magnitude claim in the explanation is contradicted and the false-positive location is overstated. The label and predicate themselves are fine, and I found no systematic false-positive class that a better predicate would fix.
